questions.q: If all the numbers which are greater than 6000 and less than 10000 are formed with the digits $3,5,6,7,8$ without repetition of the digits, then the difference between the number of odd numbers and the number of even numbers among them is
questions.solution:
Number greater than 6000 and less than 10000 is a
4-digit number cannot start from 3,5
Now, even number can onily end with 6 or 8
Total number between $6000-10000$ ending with 6
$={ }^2 \mathrm{C}_1 \times{ }^3 \mathrm{P}_2 \times 6=2!\times 3!=12$
Total even numbers $=12+12=24$
And, odd numbers can only end with $3,5,7$
Total numbers ending with $3={ }^3 \mathrm{C}_1 \times{ }^3 \mathrm{P}_1 \times 3=\frac{3!}{2!} \times 3!=18$
Total numbers ending with $5={ }^3 \mathrm{C}_1 \times{ }^3 \mathrm{P}_2 \times 5=\frac{3!}{2!} \times 3!=18$
Total numbers ending with $7={ }^3 \mathrm{C}_1 \times{ }^3 \mathrm{P}_2 \times 7=2!\times 3!=12$
So, total odd numbers $=18+18+12=48$
Difference between even and odd numbers
$=48-24=24={ }^4 \mathrm{P}_3$

Case II : If units place is 4

$(1,3,5)=4.3!=24$
Total number divisible by $6=18+18+24=60$.

questions.solution:

& \Rightarrow \quad n(n-10)+7(n-10)=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad(n-10)(n+7)=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad n=10,-7 \\
& \therefore \quad n=10 \\
&
\end{aligned}

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A regular polygon of $n$ sides has 170 diagonals, then $n$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$We know that,
\begin{array}{rlrl}\text{ Number of diagonals } & =\frac{n(n-3)}{2} \\ & \therefore & 170 & =\frac{n(n-3)}{2} \\ \Rightarrow & 340 & =n(n-3) \\ \Rightarrow & 20 \times 17 & =n(n-3) \\ \Rightarrow & n & =20\end{array}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A committee of 12 members is to be formed from 9 women and 8 men. The number of committees in which the women are in majority is
questions.solution:
A committee of 12 members is to be formed when women are in majority.
Case I 9 women and 3 men
$\begin{aligned} \therefore \text{ Number$ of $ways }={ }^9 C_9 \times{ }^8 C_3 & =1 \times \frac{8 \times 7 \times 6}{3 \times 2 \times 1} \\ & =56\end{aligned}$
Case II 8 women and 4 men
$\therefore$ Number of ways $={ }^9 C_8 \times{ }^8 C_4\begin{aligned} & =9 \times \frac{8 \times 7 \times 6 \times 5}{4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1} \\ & =630\end{aligned}$
Case III 7 women and 5 men
$\therefore$ Number of ways $={ }^9 C_7 \times{ }^8 C_5\begin{aligned} & =\frac{9 \times 8}{2 \times 1} \times \frac{8 \times 7 \times 6}{3 \times 2 \times 1} \\ & =36 \times 56=2016\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} \therefore \text{ Required number of ways } & =56+630+2016 \\ & =2702\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $l_1$ and $l_2$ be two lines intersecting at $P$. If $A_1, B_1, C_1$ are points on $l_1$, and $A_2, B_2, C_2, D_2, E_2$ are points on $l_2$ and if none of these coincides with $P$, then the number of triangles formed by these eight points, is :
questions.solution:
If triangle is formed including point ' $P$ ' the other points must be one from $l_1$ and other point from $l_2$. Number of triangles formed with $P$,
$n\left(E_1\right)={ }^3 C_1 \times{ }^5 C_1=15 \text{ ways } 
When $P$ is not included, Number of triangles formed
$n$\left(E_2\right) =${ }^3 C_2 \times{ }^5 C_1+{ }^3 C_1 \times{ }^5 C_2=15+15=30$
Total number of triangle $=n$\left(E_1\right)$+n$\left(E_2\right)$=15+30=45
